docs.title: Keel
docs.text:
Stop rebuilding the pipeline for every agent.

Keel is a context layer for AI agents inside vertical SaaS products. Domain events from your product go in. A bitemporal context graph per end-customer comes out. Every agent you build reads and writes it through the same five MCP tools.

You describe your vertical once, in a cartridge: ontology, event catalog, semantic rules, memory policies. Keel's core knows nothing about your domain. Your second agent connects in a day instead of weeks, because there is no second pipeline to write.

Status

0.24.0, alpha. The five tools over MCP and an HTTP JSON API (/v1), Postgres, webhook, Kafka and SQS adapters, semantic search, consolidation, an agent registry and SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Go and PHP, on the in-memory store, SQLite or MySQL (--db). See the roadmap.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
Every new agent in a SaaS product repeats the same work: extract the customer's data, normalize it, decide what "critical" means, keep its own memory, expose its own tools to the model. Four agents, four copies of the customer's context, four definitions of "critical", four memories that never talk.

Existing memory layers ingest text and documents and model memory per user or per agent. None of them start from domain events, and none model the tenant of the tenant: the end-customer of a B2B SaaS.

docs.title: How Keel is different
docs.text:
1. Cartridges. A vertical is declared in YAML plus a few ten-line handlers. The core stays generic. Write a cartridge for fleets, clinics, logistics, or your own product.
  2. Events in, not documents. Keel ingests structured facts with time: Postgres tables, webhooks, Kafka, SQS. Ingestion is deterministic and cheap. The graph is exact because it is born from events, not inferred from text.
  3. Every fact carries its provenance. Source, valid_from, valid_to, recorded_at, and who corrected it. Audit-ready by construction.
  4. Tenant of the tenant. One subgraph per end-customer, with its own permissions and expiry.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph saas ["Your SaaS"]
        pg[("Postgres outbox")]
        wh["Webhook"]
        jl[".jsonl file"]
    end
    subgraph core ["Keel core (domain-agnostic)"]
        env["Event envelope<br/>tenant · type · subject · time"]
        ing["Ingestor<br/>dispatch by event.type"]
        store[("Bitemporal graph<br/>one subgraph per tenant")]
        tools["Five tools<br/>context · history · search · annotate · related"]
        env --> ing --> store --> tools
    end
    subgraph cart ["Cartridge (your vertical)"]
        yaml["cartridge.yaml<br/>ontology · events · rules · memory policy"]
        hand["handlers.py<br/>payload → store primitives"]
    end
    pg & wh & jl --> env
    hand -.-> ing
    yaml -.-> tools
    tools <--> a1["Agent A"] & a2["Agent B"] & a3["Agent N"]

Events are the truth and the graph is derived, so one tenant's subgraph can be rebuilt by replaying its log. Agents never see a pipeline: they see five tools.

docs.title: Five tools, any agent
docs.text:
context(subject, as_of?, depth?, as_known_at?, task?, detail?, exclude?, only?)
  -> what is true now, at as_of, or as known at a past moment; rules and their verdicts;
     depth=1 adds the neighbors; detail="concise" for about a third of the tokens; only=[...] just those predicates
history(subject?, since?, until?, predicate?, scope?, as_known_at?, task?, changed_since?, limit?)
  -> what was true and when we learned it; without a subject, what changed since a watermark
search(text?, kind?, rule?, limit?, after?, mode?, min_score?, related_to?, via?, detail?, depth?, per_kind?, exclude?, as_of?, where?)
  -> text or semantic search, or every entity of a kind / where a rule fires, paged;
     related_to (and via) keeps only one subject's neighbors; detail="concise" puts each result's facts in it;
     per_kind=n the best of every kind: the context for a task in one call
     where={name: value} by an attribute's or a fact's value; each result says what matched (matched, snippet);
     kind may be a list of kinds
annotate(subject, predicate, value, scope?, evidence?, by?, task?, key?, status?)
  -> an agent (or a person) writes what it learned; key makes retries safe; status="proposed" waits for review
related(subject, relation?, as_of?, depth?)
  -> neighbors by relation type, up to three hops

search(mode="semantic") finds subjects by meaning: ids in the query first, then a dense and a lexical leg fused, then an optional reranker. Where vectors live and which model makes them are adapters you choose: in memory, Chroma, any OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint, or your own vector database and model (how, example).

Expose them over MCP with keel serve and point any agent framework at them. The names and signatures are part of the public standard; see the specification.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/angelkurten/keel && cd keel
uv sync --extra dev
uv run keel validate examples/fleet
uv run keel ingest examples/fleet examples/fleet/events.jsonl
uv run keel context examples/fleet examples/fleet/events.jsonl unit:MXK-4821

Then:

  • Your first cartridge in 20 minutes: declare your own vertical.
  • Connect your events: a Postgres outbox table, a webhook, Kafka, SQS or a .jsonl file; the MCP server and the HTTP JSON API; semantic search.
  • SDKs: a typed client generated from your cartridge (TypeScript, Python, Go, PHP), the way protoc does.
  • Specification: the normative contract for the envelope, the graph model, cartridges, tools and scopes.

docs.title: Design rules the core enforces
docs.text:
• Events are the truth. An append-only log. The graph is derived and can be replayed.
  • Pointers, not copies. The graph holds references to your rows, the semantics, and earned memory. Never a copy of your tables.
  • Explicit time. Facts close. They are not overwritten.
  • Scopes, not a flat store. global > tenant > task > agent. Nothing is promoted to a wider scope by accident. Agent memory is read only by the agent that wrote it; task memory tied to a task id only by calls that pass that task (context(task=), history(task=)); global memory lives in a reserved partition every tenant reads and no event writes.
  • Five tools, and only five. New capability goes into the semantics of the existing five.

docs.title: Keel specification
docs.text:
Version 0.24 · 2026-10-17 · Status: normative for the 0.24.x line; anything marked planned is not implemented yet.

This document is the contract. CLAUDE.md says how to work on the code; README.md says why Keel exists. If the code and this document disagree, one of them is wrong; open an issue.

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY are used as in RFC 2119.

docs.title: 1. Scope and terms
docs.text:
Keel is a context layer for AI agents inside a vertical SaaS. It turns domain events into a bitemporal context graph per tenant, declared by a cartridge, and exposes it to agents through five tools.

Term Meaning SaaS The product that runs Keel. Has its own database and its own customers. Tenant One end-customer of the SaaS (the tenant of the tenant). Every graph is partitioned by tenant. Event A fact that happened in the SaaS, with world time and source, in the standard envelope (§2). Subject The entity an event or fact is about, as <kind>:<id>. Entity A node in the graph: a kind, an id, a pointer (ref) to the system of record, and a few label attributes. Relation A typed, time-bounded edge between two entities. Fact A time-bounded (predicate, value) about a subject, with provenance. Cartridge The declaration of a domain: ontology, event catalog, handlers, rules, memory policy (§5). Handler Cartridge code that maps one event type's payload to store primitives (§4). Scope The sharing level of a fact: global, tenant, task, agent (§6). Tool One of the five operations agents use to read and write the graph (§7).

docs.title: 2. Event envelope
docs.text:
Every event, from any adapter, MUST be an envelope with these fields.

Field Type Req. Meaning id string no The source's own id when it has one. Otherwise a content hash of tenant, type, subject, occurred_at, source and payload, so the same stream yields the same ids on replay and a duplicate is recognizable. Used as evidence on derived facts. tenant string yes Tenant key. Opaque to Keel. type string yes Dotted lowercase event type from the cartridge catalog, e.g. inspection.created. subject string yes <kind>:<id>. kind MUST be an entity kind declared in the cartridge. occurred_at datetime (tz-aware) yes When it happened in the world. Valid time. recorded_at datetime (tz-aware) no When Keel received it. Transaction time. Defaults to now (UTC). source string yes System of record or adapter, e.g. fleet.vehicles, webhook:telematics. payload object no Event-specific data. The core MUST NOT read it. Only handlers do.

Rules:

  • Naive datetimes MUST be rejected or coerced to UTC at the envelope; they MUST NOT reach a handler.
  • occurred_at MAY be in the past relative to earlier events (late-arriving data). Handlers MUST use occurred_at as valid_from, never recorded_at.
  • Envelopes are immutable. An error in an event is corrected by a later event or by an annotate with corrected_by, never by editing the log.
  • Serialized form is JSON, one object per event. The reference development adapter reads one envelope per line (.jsonl), ignoring blank lines and lines starting with #.

docs.title: 3. Graph model
docs.text: The store holds three kinds of records, each partitioned by tenant. There is no record that spans tenants.

docs.title: 3.1 Entity
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning tenant string Partition key. kind string Entity kind from the cartridge ontology. id string Id within the kind. key = <kind>:<id>. ref string? Pointer to the row in the system of record (<source>#<id> by convention). attrs object Label attributes a tool needs to show the entity (plate, name). Never a copy of the row.

upsert_entity creates or updates in place. Entities are not bitemporal; their history is carried by facts and relations.

docs.title: 3.2 Relation
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning tenant, src, rel, dst string Edge from entity key src to entity key dst of type rel. valid_from datetime World time the relation started. valid_to datetime? World time it ended. null = open. recorded_at datetime When Keel learned it. source string? Provenance.

link is idempotent on an open edge with the same (src, rel, dst). unlink closes the open edge by setting valid_to. Edges are never deleted.

docs.title: 3.3 Fact
docs.text:
Field Type Meaning tenant, subject string Partition and entity key. predicate string What is asserted, e.g. depth_mm, status, damage:D2. value any JSON The asserted value. valid_from datetime World time the fact became true. valid_to datetime? World time it stopped being true. null = open. recorded_at datetime When Keel learned it. source string? Adapter or annotate:<by>. scope enum global, tenant, task, agent (§6). Default tenant. evidence string? Event id, row ref, photo URL or other pointer that justifies the fact. corrected_by string? A person or agent id when the fact is a correction or an annotation. expires_at datetime? Memory lifetime (not world time). Set from the scope's TTL, or to the close time when its task closes. closed_at datetime? Transaction time of the close: when Keel learned valid_to. With recorded_at it makes "as known at" queries possible. task string? The job a task-scope annotation belongs to (annotate(task=)). idempotency_key string? annotate(key=): a retried write with the same key returns this fact. status string? null = accepted (the truth rules and context.facts read); proposed = waiting for a decision; rejected = a decision, closed at once. trace string? The caller's W3C traceparent and tool call id at write time (HTTP traceparent / X-Keel-Tool-Call headers, MCP _meta), so a Langfuse or LangSmith trace joins the audit export.

Bitemporal rule. open_fact(subject, predicate, value, valid_from) MUST place the new fact in the predicate's history by valid_from: it closes the fact current at that instant (valid_to = valid_from) and, when a later fact already exists, closes itself at that fact's start. Arrival order does not change the result (§4). A predicate's history is one slot per memory scope: a fact never closes one of another scope, so a private note does not end a shared diagnosis and a promotion leaves the narrower fact to its own lifetime. Task memory has one slot per task, agent memory one per writing agent, and with per_source=True (multi-valued predicates and proposals) one per author. Facts are never mutated or deleted by handlers. The store MAY physically drop facts whose expires_at has passed (consolidation, §8).

sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Handler
    participant S as Store
    participant Q as Tool
    H->>S: open_fact(tire:T-9001, depth_mm, 5.2, valid_from=Sep 10)
    Note over S: depth_mm=5.2 valid [Sep 10, open)
    H->>S: open_fact(tire:T-9001, depth_mm, 2.6, valid_from=Oct 3)
    Note over S: close 5.2 with valid_to=Oct 3, append 2.6 valid [Oct 3, open)
    Q->>S: facts(at=Sep 20)
    S-->>Q: depth_mm=5.2
    Q->>S: facts(at=now)
    S-->>Q: depth_mm=2.6

Queries the store MUST answer:

  • facts true at a world time t: valid_from <= t < valid_to (or open).
  • facts between since and until (overlap).
  • facts as known at a transaction time t (facts(known_at=t)): recorded by t, with closes counted only when closed_at <= t (§7.6).

Values are for what a tool compares or shows. A long text (a comment body, a description, a document) belongs in the system of record: store a short label or a classification as the value and the pointer as evidence or in the entity's ref, not the text itself. The graph holds pointers and semantics (design rule 2).

docs.title: 3.4 Store protocol
docs.text:
Writes (the only write path; handlers call these and nothing else):

upsert_entity(tenant, kind, id, ref=None, **attrs) -> Entity
link(tenant, src, rel, dst, valid_from, source=None) -> Relation
unlink(tenant, src, rel, dst, valid_to) -> None
open_fact(tenant, subject, predicate, value, valid_from, **provenance) -> Fact
close_fact(tenant, subject, predicate, valid_to, status=None, scope="tenant") -> None
    # status: only proposals, or only rejections; scope: only that scope's facts (None: every scope).
    # The tenant default is what a handler means: it never closes agent or task memory.

open_fact provenance keywords: source, scope, evidence, corrected_by, expires_at, recorded_at, task, idempotency_key, status, trace, and per_source (one history per author, §3.3). A store MUST reject a second fact with the same idempotency_key on a subject by raising DuplicateKey (carrying the fact already written), atomically, so two writers racing on one key write once; the SQL stores do it with a unique index.

Reads:

entity(tenant, key) -> Entity | None
facts(tenant, subject, at=None, since=None, until=None, known_at=None) -> [Fact]
entities(tenant, kind=None) -> [Entity]
relations(tenant, key, rel=None, at=None) -> [Relation]
search(tenant, text) -> [Entity | Fact]
changes(tenant, after) -> [Fact]               # recorded or closed after a watermark, oldest change first
watermark(tenant) -> datetime | None           # optional: latest recorded_at or closed_at
relation_changes(tenant, after) -> [Relation]  # optional: links recorded after a watermark (keel index)
facts_of(tenant, subjects, **filters) -> {subject: [Fact]}   # optional: facts() for many subjects at once
entities_of(tenant, keys) -> {key: Entity | None}           # optional: entity() for many keys at once
relations_of(tenant, keys, at=None) -> {key: [Relation]}    # optional: relations() for many keys at once

Tools calls entities and changes on every store. known_at is passed only when a caller asks for transaction time, so a store without it still serves every other read. Global-scope memory is stored under the reserved tenant __global__ (§6); a store needs nothing special for it.

Ingest bookkeeping (called by the Ingestor, never by handlers): seen(tenant, event_id) and remember(tenant, event_id), the dedupe behind at-least-once delivery; reset forgets them too. A store MAY offer transaction(), a context manager the Ingestor wraps each event or batch in. Maintenance (jobs and operators): expire(tenant, now), close_task(tenant, task, now) (expires a task's memory at once), reset(tenant), dump(tenant) (everything about one tenant, closed facts included; keel export writes it as JSONL), and, optionally, tenants() (every tenant with something stored, never __global__; --all-tenants on the jobs). Erasure, optional but required by the Ingestor when the cartridge declares an event that forgets: tenant: forget(tenant) -> {entities, relations, facts, annotations, ingested} deletes, in one transaction, everything stored for the tenant (facts of every scope, annotations, dedupe marks) and leaves a tombstone (the tenant and the time); it is idempotent, keeps the first tombstone's time and refuses __global__. forgotten(tenant) -> datetime | None reads the tombstone and forgotten_tenants() -> {tenant: datetime} lists them.

A store implementation MUST pass tests/test_core.py and tests/test_store.py unchanged. Run the suite against your own store with KEEL_STORE=your_pkg.module:factory uv run pytest tests/test_store.py, where factory is a zero-argument callable (or class) returning a fresh, empty store. Reference: keel/store/memory.py (in memory). Durable: keel/store/sql.py holds one plain-SQL implementation with the same filters as the reference, and keel/store/sqlite.py (one file, WAL) and keel/store/mysql.py (MySQL or MariaDB, mysql:// URL) are its dialects; all answer identically and the conformance suite runs on SQLite and MySQL in CI. A Graphiti-backed store remains planned for graph-native queries.

docs.title: 4. Ingestion
docs.text:
The ingestor reads envelopes from an adapter and dispatches each to the handlers registered for its type.

  • The event log is the source of truth. Keel's own copy of the log (Ingestor.log, opt-in with keep_log=True) is a development convenience that grows with every event; in production the bus holds it.
  • Dispatch is deterministic: no network, no LLM, no randomness in the ingest path. Replaying the same log in the same order MUST produce an identical graph.
  • An event with no handler is reported as unhandled; in strict mode it raises. A handler exception is reported with the event id and does not stop the stream, unless strict.
  • replay(tenant, events=None) wipes that tenant's event-derived subgraph (entities, relations, facts from handlers, dedupe marks) and re-dispatches its events from the external log given (the bus, the outbox table, a stream) or, without one, from the in-memory log (only kept with Ingestor(..., keep_log=True); otherwise replay without events is an error). It keeps annotations (facts whose source is annotate:... or consolidate:..., closed history included): they are earned memory, not in the log, and the events land around them as they did the first time (a store's reset(tenant, keep_annotations=True)). It is the recovery path, not the update path.
  • Ordering: adapters SHOULD deliver events in occurred_at order per subject, but the result MUST NOT depend on it for facts: open_fact places a fact in its predicate's history by valid_from, closing the fact current at that instant and closing itself at the next fact's start, so a late event lands in its slot instead of closing a newer fact backwards. Relations (link/unlink) still assume order per subject.
  • Transactions: when the store has them (the SQL stores do), each event is applied in one, so the handler's primitives and the dedupe mark land together (remember runs first, in the same transaction, and is one statement); a bulk caller passes batch= to commit every n events (the CLI and the HTTP batch do), and a chunk that raises in strict mode is rolled back whole and redelivered whole. A streaming adapter is never buffered.
  • Batches: a store MAY offer bulk(events), a context manager the Ingestor uses for chunks larger than one event. The SQL stores read the state of the chunk's subjects in a few statements, serve the handlers from memory, and write back in a few multi-row statements; the result is the same as event by event (the conformance suite checks it on every store, forwards and shuffled), about a thousand times fewer round trips.
  • Batch reads: a store MAY offer facts_of, entities_of and relations_of, the same answers as facts and entity for many subjects. context(depth=1) reads its neighbours with them, search(rule=) its candidates in chunks, and a rule that follows a relation its neighbours: a few statements whatever the neighbourhood's size, where one per subject would be a round trip each on a networked database. Without them Tools reads one subject at a time.
  • Threads: a store shared by a server's threads MUST keep a transaction, its read cache and a batch in flight to the thread that opened them: another thread waits for it or reads committed state, and never writes into it (a write that joined a batch would be lost with its rollback). The MySQL store reads on one connection per thread, so reads never queue behind a writer.
  • Erasure: an event whose type the cartridge declares forgets: tenant runs no handler; the Ingestor calls store.forget(tenant) in that event's transaction (a chunk holding one is applied event by event, never through bulk) and lists what was deleted in IngestReport.forgotten. Every later event for a forgotten tenant, a late redelivery included, is skipped without being applied and counted in IngestReport.skipped, so nothing revives it, and a replay of it yields nothing. Keel deletes only what it stores: the external log (the bus, the outbox table) belongs to the SaaS, and global memory (§6) is every tenant's and is kept.
  • Duplicates: an event whose id the store has already applied for that tenant is skipped and counted in IngestReport.duplicates. With content-hash ids this makes at-least-once adapters and client retries safe; a source that can emit two identical events at the same instant MUST give them ids.

docs.title: 4.1 Adapters
docs.text:
An adapter is any iterable of envelopes. It MUST NOT interpret payloads.

Adapter Status Notes JSONL file shipped Development and tests. Postgres table + polling shipped PostgresTableAdapter: a seq cursor in a file, so restarts resume; it moves only after the Ingestor commits (ack()). At-least-once. Webhook (HTTP) shipped build_app: validates the envelope, ingests, returns the report; bearer token. Kafka shipped KafkaAdapter (keel.adapters.bus): offset committed after the Ingestor commits the batch (ack()). At-least-once; dead_letter for poison messages. SQS shipped SqsAdapter (keel.adapters.bus): message deleted after the Ingestor commits the batch (ack()). Same semantics. keel consume --queue <url> runs it, one transaction per message; a failed message stays for the queue's dead-letter queue. Postgres CDC planned

docs.title: 4.2 Handlers
docs.text:
A handler is fn(event, store) -> None, registered for one event type with @registry.on("<type>"). It:

  • MUST only call store primitives (§3.4).
  • MUST use event.occurred_at for valid_from/valid_to.
  • SHOULD pass source=event.source and evidence=event.id on every fact.
  • MUST NOT contain business definitions (what "critical" means). Those are rules (§5.4).
  • SHOULD be about ten lines.

docs.title: 5. Cartridge format
docs.text: A cartridge is a directory with cartridge.yaml and handlers.py.

docs.title: 5.1 cartridge.yaml
docs.text:
name: <slug>            # required
version: <semver>       # optional, recommended

entities:               # required: kind -> spec
  <kind>:
    description: <text>
    ref: <table.column> # optional, documents where `ref` points

relations:              # optional: rel -> {from: <kind>, to: <kind>}
  <rel>: { from: <kind>, to: <kind> }
  <rel>: { from: <kind>, to: <kind>, symmetric: true }   # recorded from either end, shown once (direction `both`)

events:                 # required: type -> spec
  <type>:
    subject: <kind>     # required: the kind of event.subject
    owner: <team>       # recommended: who owns this event's shape
    payload: { <field>: <hint>, ... }   # the notation in §5.5; `| null` = optional
    forgets: tenant     # optional: this event erases its tenant (§4); it takes no handler

rules:                  # optional: name -> definition
  <rule>:
    applies_to: <kind>  # optional; absent = applies to every subject
    definition: <text>  # human-readable, versioned with the cartridge
    <param>: <value>    # machine-readable parameters agents read
    when:               # optional: a condition the core evaluates in `context` (§5.4)
      predicate: <predicate>
      <op>: <operand>   # leaf operators in §5.4; compose with all / any / not; follow relations with via

predicates:             # optional: write policy per predicate, for annotations
  <predicate>: { multi: true, description: <text> }   # multi: one open value per author (the `by`, else the agent) instead of last-writer-wins; context lists conflicts

semantic:               # optional: what `keel index` puts in each subject's document (§7.3)
  kinds: [<kind>, ...]           # absent: every kind
  predicates: [<predicate>, ...] # what to include; or exclude: [<predicate>, ...]
  attrs: true                    # entity attributes (default); false, or a list of names
  relations: [<rel>, ...]        # open relations: the other side's key and one label
  labels: [name, nombre]         # the attribute that labels the other side (first present wins); default: name, nombre, title, titulo, label, plate, model
  lexical_weight: 0.3            # hybrid search: weight of the lexical leg (0 = dense only)
  min_score: 0.4                 # optional cosine floor; model-specific, calibrate with evals/semantic
  split: { <kind>: [<predicate>, ...] }  # also one document per open fact of these predicates, and per element of a list value (each field of a visual), not only one per subject

consolidate:            # optional: episodic memory summarized into durable facts (§8)
  <name>:
    from: { predicate: <p>, scopes: [task] }   # default [task]; agent memory is read only when listed
    applies_to: <kind>             # optional
    within: 30d                    # optional window on valid_from (world time)
    min_count: 3                   # default 2
    reduce: mode                   # mode | latest | count | min | max | avg | distinct | summary
    into: { predicate: <q>, scope: tenant }

calendar:               # optional: business days for `open_for_business_days` (§5.4)
  weekend: [saturday, sunday]
  holidays: [2026-12-25]

agents:                 # optional: the agent registry (§6.1). Absent = no registry, any caller
  <id>:
    description: <text>
    kind: agent                                  # or human: a person, signed human:<id> (§6.1)
    writes: [task, agent]                        # scopes it may annotate; never global; absent = [task, agent]
    reads: { kinds: [<kind>, ...], relations: [<rel>, ...] }   # optional; absent = everything

memory:                 # optional; defaults in §6
  ttl:
    global: never | forever | <n>d | <n>h | <n>m | <n>   # a bare number is days
    tenant: never | ...
    task: 14d
    agent: 1d
  requires_evidence: [global, tenant]

docs.title: 5.2 handlers.py
docs.text: MUST define registry = HandlerRegistry() at module level with one or more @registry.on(...) functions.

docs.title: 5.3 Validation (keel validate)
docs.text:
A cartridge is valid when:

  1. every relation's from and to are declared entity kinds;
  2. every event's subject is a declared entity kind;
  3. every cataloged event type has at least one handler, except one that forgets: tenant, which has none (forgets takes only tenant);
  4. every handler's event type is in the catalog;
  5. every rule's when names a predicate and uses only the operators in §5.4;
  6. every agent's kind is agent or human, its writes are known scopes other than global, and its reads name declared kinds and relations;
  7. every event's payload hints use the notation in §5.5;
  8. predicates, semantic and consolidate use only known keys, with values in range (a weight between 0 and 1, a known reducer, a known scope);
  9. every via names a declared relation with a valid direction, and duration operators (open_for_*, held_for_*) take a comparison mapping.

keel validate <cartridge> --events <stream.jsonl> also checks every envelope in the stream against the catalog: the type is cataloged, the subject's kind is the event's subject, and each declared payload field is present with its declared shape (§5.5; | null makes it optional). It looks at payload keys and types, never at values; it is the one place the core looks at a payload at all.

docs.title: 5.4 Rules (semantic layer)
docs.text:
Rules are authored by product, versioned with the cartridge, and returned by the context tool for the subject's kind. Agents MUST read definitions from rules rather than hard-code them. The core interprets two keys: applies_to and when. context evaluates every applicable rule that has a when at as_of and returns true, false, or null (undecidable). A rule without when (an aggregate, a count over time) is returned as a definition only and the agent applies it.

A when is a condition:

  • Leaf: { predicate: <p>, <op>: <operand>, ... }. Operators on the subject's open fact for <p>: lt, lte, gt, gte, eq, ne, in (value in a list), within_days (a date predicate on or before as_of + n days, so dates already past count), open_for_days and open_for_business_days (how long the open fact has been open: a mapping of lt/lte/gt/gte/eq, e.g. { gte: 7 }; business days skip the cartridge calendar weekend and holidays), held_for_days and held_for_business_days (how long the leaf's comparison has held across consecutive facts of the predicate: a waiting clock that survives a change from one waiting status to another; without a comparison, how long the predicate has had any value without a gap). ci: true compares strings case-insensitively. No open fact for the predicate: null.
  • Composition: { all: [...] }, { any: [...] }, { not: <condition> }. A bare list is all. null propagates unless another branch decides: a false in all, a true in any.
  • Neighbours: { via: <relation>, direction: out | in | any, any: <condition> } or all:. The condition is evaluated on each neighbour reached by that relation at as_of (direction defaults to any; symmetric relations ignore it). No neighbours: any is false, all is true. This is how an inherited state is expressed: { any: [ { predicate: status, eq: paused }, { via: relates_to, any: { predicate: status, eq: paused } } ] }.

Rules see the whole tenant's graph: they are the product's semantics, not the calling agent's view, so the agent registry's read slice does not apply inside a when.

docs.title: 5.5 Payload notation
docs.text:
The payload: mapping of an event is a schema in a short notation. Keel checks streams against it (keel validate --events) and prints it as JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (keel schema <cartridge>), which is what SDK templates read.

Written as Means JSON Schema string, int, number, bool a scalar type string / integer / number / boolean date, datetime an ISO 8601 string type: string with format any anything {} <hint> \| null optional and nullable type: [<type>, "null"], not in required string[] (any scalar) array of scalars type: array, items [pending, paid] enum of literals enum [new, done, null] optional enum (null is a literal in the list; | null is not YAML here) enum with null, not in required [ { id: string, qty: int } ] array of objects type: array, items: object { source: string, score: number } nested object type: object, properties, required

Extra fields in a payload are allowed: the catalog documents what handlers need, not everything the source sends. An unknown hint is a validation error, so a typo never passes as any; [string] is rejected in favour of string[].

docs.title: 5.6 The generality test
docs.text: Adding or changing a cartridge MUST require no change under keel/. The repository keeps four cartridges (fleet, crm, finance, clinics) and all MUST pass the test suite after any core change.

docs.title: 6. Memory scopes and policy
docs.text:
Scope Who reads Who writes Default TTL Evidence required global every tenant's agents a privileged process (a Tools bound to no registry agent; never an agent, never an event) never yes tenant that tenant's agents handlers (from events); agents/humans via annotate never yes task calls that pass the fact's task (context(task=), history(task=)); a task fact with no task id is the tenant's agents via annotate 14 days no agent the agent that wrote it (a Tools bound to no agent id reads none) that agent 1 day no 
flowchart LR
    g["global<br/>every tenant · never expires · evidence"] --> t["tenant<br/>one end-customer · never expires · evidence"] --> k["task<br/>agents on one task · 14 d"] --> a["agent<br/>one agent · 1 d"]
    w["annotate(subject, predicate, value, scope, evidence, by)"] --> p{"MemoryPolicy.check_write"}
    p -- "scope requires evidence, none given" --> e["PermissionError"]
    p -- "ok" --> f["open_fact with scope, evidence, corrected_by=by<br/>expires_at = now + ttl"]

Rules:

  • Policy is enforced in Tools.annotate via MemoryPolicy.check_write; the calling agent is not trusted to self-police.
  • A write to a scope that requires evidence without evidence MUST raise PermissionError.
  • Facts written by handlers from events are tenant scope with evidence = event.id.
  • Promotion to a wider scope is a new annotate with evidence and by; the narrower fact keeps its own lifetime.
  • expires_at = now + ttl at write time; null when TTL is never. Reads MUST exclude expired facts even before a job physically removes them.
  • Reads are enforced in Tools, on every path that returns facts (context and its neighbours, rule evaluation, history with or without a subject, text search): an agent fact is returned only to a caller bound to its author (its source is annotate:<author>); a task fact tied to a task only to calls passing that task; a task fact with no task id to the whole tenant. Rules evaluate on the same view, so another agent's or another task's memory never decides a verdict.
  • Global memory lives in the reserved partition __global__: annotate(scope="global") writes there and every tenant's reads merge it, so one fact is seen by every tenant. No event may carry that tenant and no Tools may be bound to it. It is the one deliberate exception to invariant 1, and it holds only what a privileged process wrote.

docs.title: 6.1 Agent registry
docs.text:
A cartridge MAY declare agents: (§5.1). Without it there is no registry: any caller, any scope with evidence, and an agent id passed to Tools is attribution only. With it:

  • A Tools instance MUST be bound to a declared agent (Tools(..., agent=<id>), keel serve --agent <id>). A missing or unknown id raises PermissionError at construction.
  • Writes. annotate to a scope outside the agent's writes raises PermissionError. global is never writable by an agent. The scope policy (evidence, TTL) applies after the registry check. source is annotate:<agent>; corrected_by is by when given (a human correcting through the agent), else the agent id.
  • People. An entry with kind: human is a person: it is enforced like any agent, and its annotations are signed annotate:human:<id> with corrected_by = human:<id>. Approvals are writes by a declared person, so the audit export shows who approved.
  • Reads. context, history, related and annotate on a subject whose kind is outside reads.kinds raise PermissionError. Relations outside reads.relations, or whose other end is a hidden kind, are left out of context and related. search drops hits on hidden kinds.
  • Authentication is the host's job. Keel takes the agent id as given and enforces what that id may do; it never trusts the agent to police itself (rule 5).

docs.title: 7. The five tools
docs.text: A Tools instance is bound to one cartridge, one tenant and, when the cartridge declares agents, one agent (§6.1). Cross-tenant access does not exist at this layer. These five names and argument orders are part of the public standard; adding a sixth is a spec change.

docs.title: 7.1 context(subject, as_of=None, depth=0, as_known_at=None, task=None, detail="full", exclude=None, only=None) -> object
docs.text:
subject may be a list: the answers come back in order, one per subject, in one call. exclude (a list of predicates) leaves those predicates out of facts, proposals and the neighbours' facts, for an evaluation in which the agent must not see the answer; rules still evaluate on the whole truth, so a verdict can reveal it. only (a non-empty list of predicates) is the opposite: just those predicates, in the same places, for the evidence a reviewer checks across many subjects without the rest of their facts; exclude still hides what it names. A list of subjects is read in a few statements (facts, proposals, relations and entities in batches), not one or more per subject. A search with a list of texts shares those reads too: each subject's facts are read once for every text, so checking many names against one subject's neighbours (search(names, kind=[...], related_to=s)) is one call.

facts holds accepted facts only. proposals (present when any) holds the open proposals; conflicts (present when any) maps each predicate that has more than one open value to those values and their authors, which happens for multi predicates (§5.1) written by several agents. detail="concise" returns the same answer for a prompt in about a third of the tokens: attrs, facts as {predicate: value} (a list of {value, by} for a multi-valued one), relations as {relation, direction, subject} (direction both for a symmetric relation, as everywhere else), evaluation, as_of, watermark, proposals and conflicts, and compact neighbours; rule definitions are left out (their names are in evaluation).

What is true about a subject now, or at as_of (world time). With depth=1 the answer also carries neighbors: for each open relation (up to 50, then neighbors_truncated: true), the other subject's entity, open facts and rule evaluation, so one call brings a card and the cards it is linked to.

{
  "subject": "unit:MXK-4821",
  "entity": { "kind": "unit", "id": "MXK-4821", "ref": "fleet.vehicles#MXK-4821", "attrs": {...} },
  "facts": [ ...open facts at now, expired excluded... ],
  "relations": [ ...open relations at now, both directions... ],
  "rules": { "<rule>": {...} },      // rules with applies_to == subject kind or absent
  "evaluation": { "<rule>": true },  // true | false | null, for the rules above that carry a `when`
  "as_of": "2026-10-14T18:41:07Z"    // now, or the `as_of` asked for
}

docs.title: 7.2 history(subject=None, since=None, until=None, predicate=None, scope=None, as_known_at=None, task=None, changed_since=None, limit=None) -> [Fact]
docs.text: Facts over time, oldest first, including closed ones. predicate, scope and task filter (task returns only what that task wrote; without it, task memory tied to a task is not returned, §6); limit keeps the most recent n, still oldest first (ask for one more to know whether more exist). as_known_at returns the facts as Keel knew them then (§7.6). changed_since keeps the facts recorded or closed after a watermark; with no subject it spans the tenant (subjects the caller may read), ordered by the time of the change: the "since my last run" read of an incremental agent. Each fact carries valid_from, valid_to, recorded_at, closed_at, source, evidence, scope, corrected_by, task.

docs.title: 7.3 search(text="", kind=None (or a list), rule=None, limit=None, after=None, mode="text", min_score=None, related_to=None, via=None, detail="entity", depth=0, per_kind=None, exclude=None, as_of=None, where=None) -> [Entity | Fact]
docs.text:
What each entity result carries: detail="entity" (the default) the entity; "concise" also its current facts as {predicate: value}, "full" as facts, so a result needs no context call to be understood. depth=1 adds neighbors (relation, direction, subject, and their facts when detail asks for them; up to 50, then neighbors_truncated). Facts and neighbours of a page are read in a few statements whatever its size. per_kind=n returns the best n of every kind instead of one ranking (in semantic mode one ranking per kind, rule or kind narrowing the kinds; in text mode the text ranking cut per kind; not with after): with related_to for the scope, mode="semantic" and detail="concise", the context a task needs in one call. exclude leaves predicates out of what is returned and drops fact hits on them. as_of evaluates rule, walks related_to and reads the facts and neighbours at that instant (entities are not bitemporal; the semantic index is as of its last keel index). text may be a list: one result list per text, in order. kind may be a list: the listing covers those kinds, ordered by key (after is then a full key), a semantic ranking only them, and per_kind the best n of each (in text mode, the first n of each listing; one kind with per_kind in text mode is an error, that is limit).

where={name: value} keeps the entities whose attribute name, or current accepted fact name (at as_of), is value, or a list holding it; strings compare without case, and the whole value, not a part of it: search(kind="visual", where={"title": "Detalhe Ociosidade"}) finds a visual by its exact title, which a semantic search blurs. It applies in every mode, after the other filters; a name that exclude hides is an error. Each ranked entity says why it is a result: matched is the attribute or predicate whose value matched (or "key"), and snippet the part of that value around the match (up to 160 characters; of a list, the element). In text mode that is the substring; in semantic mode, the split document that ranked it (below) or else the field sharing most words with the query; nothing when no field does, and never a hidden predicate. A listing without text carries neither.

related_to (a subject key the caller may read) keeps only that subject's current neighbours, through relation via when given, in every mode: search(kind="card", rule="en_pausa", related_to="cliente:BAT", via="de_cliente") is the paused cards of one client in one call, walking the client's neighbours rather than the whole kind. after has one format, the key of the last entity received (tire:T-9002); an id alone is accepted when the listing has one kind. It pages the kind/rule listing only: with mode="semantic" or a plain text search it is an error, since those rank and page with limit.

Every entity the tools return (here, in context.entity, in neighbors, and in keel export) carries key, the <kind>:<id> that every other call takes and that after expects.

Without kind and rule: case-insensitive substring match over entity keys and attrs, and fact predicates and values. With kind, or rule (whose applies_to gives the kind, and which must carry a when): the entities of that kind whose key, attrs or current facts' values match text (since 0.20; before, key and attrs only), and with rule only those where the rule evaluates true now, ordered by key; limit caps the page and after (the last key received) continues it. This is the work list of a sweep, a router or an orchestrator.

mode="semantic" ranks subjects by meaning: subjects whose id appears verbatim in the query come first (match: "key", score 1); then a dense leg (the embedded query against the vector index) and, when the index offers text_query, a lexical leg (BM25 over the same documents) are fused by a convex combination of min-max normalized scores, weighted by the cartridge's semantic.lexical_weight (default 0.3; 0 is dense only); then the optional reranker reorders the top candidates. The tenant, the agent's read slice, kind and rule always apply, inside the index when its query takes where; with related_to, where also carries subject (the neighbours' keys; a split document belongs to its subject), which an index MAY apply and Keel checks after retrieval either way. Each entity carries score and similarity (the cosine); min_score (or the cartridge's semantic.min_score) drops results below that cosine, and is model-specific. Default limit 10. Three adapter contracts make it pluggable (keel.semantic): VectorIndex (upsert, delete, query, clear, always by tenant, an index never returns another tenant's keys; optional where on query and an optional text_query), Embedder (embed(texts), optionally role="query"|"document" for asymmetric models) and Reranker (rerank(query, docs); bundled: the Cohere/Jina/Voyage /rerank shape and an LLM reranker over any /chat/completions). Keel ships MemoryIndex, ChromaIndex (extra chroma), WeaviateIndex (extra weaviate), OpenAIEmbedder (any /v1/embeddings API) and HashEmbedder (tests); any other is a pkg.module:factory?param=value spec, checked by tests/test_semantic.py with KEEL_VECTOR_INDEX / KEEL_EMBEDDER. The index is built by keel index, outside ingest (rule 10): one document per subject with its key, attributes, open accepted facts of tenant and global scope and the open relations the cartridge names, as chosen by the cartridge's semantic: section (§5.1); task and agent memory and proposals are never indexed; with semantic.split, each open fact of the listed predicates is also a document of its own (a list value, one per element), a hit on it ranks its subject (which keeps its best document, and says which predicate in matched and which value or element in snippet), and a changed value replaces its document; incremental from a watermark (subjects whose facts changed, and both ends of new links), --full rebuilds. A rule or kind filter never cuts the page: candidates are fetched in widening windows until limit results pass or the index runs out.

docs.title: 7.4 annotate(subject, predicate, value, scope="task", evidence=None, by=None, task=None, key=None, status=None) -> Fact
docs.text: Writes earned memory. Applies the agent registry (§6.1) and the scope policy (§6); refused for a forgotten tenant (§4). source is annotate:<agent, or by, or 'agent'> (annotate:human:<id> for a person); corrected_by is by, else the caller. task ties the fact to one job: history(task=) and context(task=) read it, and closing the task (store.close_task, keel expire --task) expires its memory at once. key makes the write idempotent, for durable-execution engines that replay steps: the same key on the same subject returns the fact it wrote; the same key with a different predicate, value, task or status raises. status="proposed" writes a proposal: it never touches accepted facts, waits in context.proposals, and needs only some write right (not the right on scope), so an agent can propose a tenant fact a person accepts; the evidence policy of scope still applies. An accepted write (no status) or status="rejected" is a decision: it needs the right on scope and closes the predicate's open proposals; a rejection is recorded closed at once, in history only. Proposals are kept one open per author per predicate, in their own history beside the accepted facts. Store close_fact takes status so handlers never close proposals. Returns the stored fact including expires_at, status and trace.

docs.title: 7.5 related(subject, relation=None, as_of=None, depth=1) -> [{relation, direction, subject, since}]
docs.text: Open relations at now or at as_of, optionally filtered by type (one, or a list), with direction relative to the subject (out, in, or both for a symmetric relation, which is reported once even when the source recorded it from both ends). depth 2 or 3 keeps walking through the same relations, nearest first and each subject once: every entry then carries hops and via, the subject it was reached from, to which its direction is relative.

docs.title: 7.6 Two time axes
docs.text: as_of is world time: what was true then. as_known_at is transaction time: what Keel knew then, which is what an agent saw when it decided. A fact counts as known at t when recorded_at <= t, its close counts only when closed_at <= t, and memory counts when it had not expired by t. context(as_known_at=t) defaults as_of to t, and also evaluates the rules on that view; relations count when recorded_at <= t. Every context carries watermark, the tenant's latest transaction time, which is the cursor an agent stores for its next history(changed_since=), passed back exactly as received. Every time argument of the five tools takes a datetime or ISO 8601 text, in every transport. Entities are not bitemporal and are shown as they are now. Facts written before 0.9 have no closed_at; their closes count as always known.

docs.title: 7.7 Transport
docs.text: The tools are plain functions first. keel serve exposes the same five over MCP (stdio, or streamable HTTP at /mcp with --transport http --tenant) and as a JSON API (POST /v1/<tool>, one process for many tenants, tenant and agent from X-Keel-Tenant and X-Keel-Agent behind a shared bearer secret). The names and semantics MUST NOT change per transport: annotate's value is any JSON over MCP, HTTP and in Python alike.

docs.title: 8. Jobs
docs.text:
• Expiry: drop facts past expires_at, per tenant. Shipped: store.expire(tenant) on both stores and keel expire <tenant> --db; the schedule is the operator's cron. Reads exclude expired facts regardless.
  • Consolidation: keel consolidate (or keel expire --consolidate, which consolidates before dropping, so nothing is lost unsummarized) runs the cartridge's consolidate: entries for a tenant: per subject, the matching episodic facts (predicate, scopes, kind, a window on valid_from; expired-but-not-dropped ones count; agent memory only when from.scopes lists it, since consolidating it promotes private memory) are reduced into one durable fact when there are at least min_count. Reducers are deterministic (mode with ties to the latest, latest, count, min, max, avg, distinct); summary asks a Summarizer adapter (LLMSummarizer over any /chat/completions, or yours) for one sentence. The fact carries source=consolidate:<name>, evidence naming the count, the span of their valid_from and the originals' evidence, and an idempotency key over its inputs: the same inputs never write twice, new inputs write a new value that closes the old. Proposals are never consolidated, and the written fact carries corrected_by=job:consolidate:<name>. The summarizer is chosen with --summarizer llm|join|pkg.module:factory; llm reads KEEL_SUMMARIZER_BASE_URL, KEEL_SUMMARIZER_MODEL and KEEL_SUMMARIZER_API_KEY. The originals are kept until their TTL. A job, never part of ingest.
  • Every tenant: keel index, keel consolidate and keel expire take --all-tenants instead of one tenant and run over store.tenants() one after another.
  • Erasure: keel forget <tenant> --db --yes [--index] erases one tenant (§3.4) and prints what it deleted as JSON; with --index its semantic documents go too. index_tenant clears a forgotten tenant's documents, and keel index --all-tenants does so for every tenant forgotten since its last run (its cursor file marks it as not yet cleared). annotate on a forgotten tenant raises.
  • Replay: rebuild a tenant from the external log. Shipped: Ingestor.replay(tenant, events=adapter) and keel replay <cartridge> <stream> <tenant> --db.

docs.title: 9. Invariants (what a conformance test checks)
docs.text:
1. No record spans tenants; every read is partitioned by tenant (global memory is read from its own partition, §6).
  2. open_fact never overwrites: after two writes to the same predicate, both facts exist and the first is closed at the second's valid_from.
  3. A fact query at=t returns exactly the facts valid at t.
  4. Replay produces a graph equal to the one built incrementally.
  5. annotate to a scope in requires_evidence without evidence raises.
  6. task/agent annotations carry expires_at; tenant/global with never TTL do not.
  7. The core imports nothing from cartridges/ or examples/; every example cartridge validates and passes after any core change.
  8. Ingest performs no I/O other than reading the adapter and writing the store.
  9. Ingesting the same event twice changes nothing, and ingesting the same events in any order yields the same facts.
  10. Scope reads hold (§6): agent memory reaches only its author, task memory only its task, global memory every tenant.

docs.title: 10. Non-goals
docs.text:
• Document or conversation ingestion (RAG memory). Keel can hold a pointer to such a store's output as a fact.
  • Agent orchestration, planning or tool routing.
  • A query language exposed to agents beyond the five tools.
  • Cross-tenant analytics (do that on the SaaS's warehouse).

docs.title: 11. Versioning
docs.text:
• The envelope, the cartridge format and the five tool signatures are versioned together as the Keel standard; breaking changes bump the minor version while pre-1.0.
  • A cartridge declares its own version; the core records which cartridge version built a tenant's graph (planned).
  • Store implementations are versioned independently; all MUST pass the conformance invariants (§9).

docs.title: Connect your events
docs.text: Keel ingests envelopes, never raw rows. Every source produces the same shape, and the cartridge's handlers are the only code that reads a payload. Pick the source that matches where your events already are.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Every setting the CLI reads from the environment can live in a .env file: keel loads ./.env when it exists, or the file named by --env-file (or KEEL_ENV_FILE). Variables already set in the environment win, so a deployment can override the file. KEY=VALUE lines, # comments, optional export and quotes; no interpolation. Copy .env.example and fill in what you use; keep .env out of git (it holds secrets).

Variable Used by What KEEL_DB every command with --db the durable graph: a SQLite file or mysql://user:pass@host:3306/db KEEL_TENANT every command that takes a tenant; serve (--tenant) the default tenant; with serve --transport http it is used when X-Keel-Tenant is absent KEEL_AGENT serve, context... (--agent) the declared agent acting here KEEL_CERTFILE, KEEL_KEYFILE serve --transport http TLS certificate and key (PEM) to serve https (--certfile, --keyfile) KEEL_SECRET serve --transport http the shared bearer secret (--secret-env names another variable) KEEL_INDEX, KEEL_EMBEDDER index, serve the vector index and embedder specs (--index, --embedder) KEEL_INDEX_CURSOR, KEEL_INDEX_WORKERS index where the cursor of the last run is kept (on a volume) and how many embedding batches go out at once (--cursor, --workers) KEEL_EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL, _MODEL, _API_KEY, _QUERY_PREFIX, _DOCUMENT_PREFIX --embedder openai any OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint KEEL_RERANK_BASE_URL, _MODEL, _API_KEY serve --reranker http\|llm the reranker endpoint KEEL_SUMMARIZER_BASE_URL, _MODEL, _API_KEY consolidate --summarizer llm the chat model that writes summaries

A flag on the command line beats both.

No end-customers? Keel keys everything on a tenant, but nothing forces you to have many. Pick one fixed value, put it in every envelope's tenant and in KEEL_TENANT=default, and stop passing --tenant: every command, keel serve and the HTTP API (no X-Keel-Tenant needed) use it. The tenant scope then simply means "shared by every agent".

The Python API reads nothing from .env: a program that embeds Keel passes its settings itself.

docs.title: The envelope
docs.text:
One event, as the development adapter reads it from examples/fleet/events.jsonl:

{"tenant": "acme-logistics", "type": "unit.registered", "subject": "unit:MXK-4821",
 "occurred_at": "2026-09-01T09:00:00Z", "source": "fleet.vehicles",
 "payload": {"id": "MXK-4821", "plate": "MXK-4821", "model": "Freightliner Cascadia"}}
Field Required Meaning tenant yes The end-customer this fact belongs to. Opaque to Keel. type yes Dotted lowercase type from the cartridge catalog. subject yes <kind>:<id> of the entity the fact is about. occurred_at yes When it happened in the world. Timezone-aware. source yes System of record or adapter name. id no Generated when absent. Becomes the evidence of derived facts. recorded_at no When Keel learned it. Defaults to now. payload no Event data. Only handlers read it.

The full rules are in the specification.

docs.title: A .jsonl file
docs.text:
For development and tests. One envelope per line; blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

uv run keel ingest examples/fleet examples/fleet/events.jsonl

The command prints processed, duplicates, unhandled, errors and skipped (events for a forgotten tenant, see Erase a tenant) and carries on past a bad event. --strict stops at the first unhandled type or handler error instead; on a SQL store the batch in flight (5000 events) is rolled back.

docs.title: A Postgres outbox table
docs.text:
Your SaaS inserts envelopes into a table. Keel polls it in order and remembers the last row it took in a cursor file, so a restart resumes instead of re-ingesting.

CREATE TABLE keel_events (
    seq          bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
    id           text NOT NULL,
    tenant       text NOT NULL,
    type         text NOT NULL,
    subject      text NOT NULL,
    occurred_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    recorded_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    source       text NOT NULL,
    payload      jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

uv sync --extra postgres

import psycopg

from keel import Ingestor, MemoryStore, SqliteStore, load_cartridge
from keel.adapters.postgres import PostgresTableAdapter

ingestor = Ingestor(load_cartridge("examples/fleet"), SqliteStore("keel.db"))  # durable; MemoryStore() for a throwaway graph
adapter = PostgresTableAdapter(lambda: psycopg.connect(DSN), table="keel_events", cursor_path=".keel/cursor")

ingestor.ingest(adapter)                      # one pass over everything after the cursor
ingestor.ingest(adapter.follow(interval=5))   # or poll forever

Delivery is at-least-once: Ingestor.ingest moves the cursor only after each commit (it calls the adapter's ack()), so with batch=N a batch that rolls back, or a crash mid-batch, is read again whole; the store skips what it already applied as duplicates. Iterating the adapter by hand, the cursor moves when you ask for the next event; call adapter.ack() after storing instead if you batch your own writes. The table name, the cursor column and the batch size are parameters (table=, cursor_column="seq", batch_size=500). Any DB-API 2.0 connection works; pass placeholder="?" for sqlite3.

sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Your SaaS
    participant T as keel_events
    participant A as PostgresTableAdapter
    participant C as cursor file
    participant I as Ingestor
    S->>T: INSERT envelope (seq 41)
    A->>C: read position
    C-->>A: 40
    A->>T: SELECT * WHERE seq > 40 ORDER BY seq LIMIT 500
    T-->>A: row 41
    A->>I: Event 41
    I->>I: dispatch to the handler
    I->>A: next event?
    A->>C: write 41
    Note over A,I: a crash before "write 41" re-delivers event 41 on restart

Concurrent writers

A serial cursor can skip a row that commits late while a later row was already read. Use one writer per table, or a recorded_at cursor with a lag, if that bites.

docs.title: A webhook
docs.text:
Keel receives envelopes over HTTP, validates them and ingests them in the request.

uv sync --extra webhook

# app.py
from keel import Ingestor, MemoryStore, SqliteStore, load_cartridge
from keel.adapters.webhook import build_app

ingestor = Ingestor(load_cartridge("examples/fleet"), SqliteStore("keel.db"))  # durable; MemoryStore() for a throwaway graph
app = build_app(ingestor, token="shared-secret")

uv run uvicorn app:app --port 8000
curl -X POST localhost:8000/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer shared-secret" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '[{"tenant": "acme-logistics", "type": "unit.registered", "subject": "unit:MXK-4821", "occurred_at": "2026-09-01T09:00:00Z", "source": "fleet.vehicles", "payload": {"id": "MXK-4821", "plate": "MXK-4821", "model": "Freightliner Cascadia"}}]'

The body is one envelope or a list. The response is the ingest report: processed, duplicates (ids the store had already applied), unhandled types, errors, forgotten (the tenants this batch erased, with what was deleted) and skipped (events for a forgotten tenant). build_app(ingestor, token=..., strict=True) fails the request at the first unhandled type or handler error instead of reporting it; on a SQL store the request's batch is rolled back, so the sender can retry it whole. A malformed envelope is a 422; a wrong token is a 401. Without a token the endpoint accepts any caller, so use that only on localhost.

docs.title: Consume a Kafka topic or an SQS queue
docs.text:
Your SaaS publishes envelopes as JSON messages; Keel consumes them. uv sync --extra kafka (confluent-kafka) or --extra sqs (boto3).

For SQS there is a command; run it as a long-lived service:

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... AWS_REGION=us-east-1 \
  uv run keel consume cartridges/mine --queue https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/keel-events --db keel.db
uv run keel consume cartridges/mine --queue http://elasticmq:9324/000000000000/keel-events --db keel.db   # SQS-compatible: the queue's host is the endpoint

Each message is one transaction and is deleted only once stored. A message that fails (not an envelope, a type with no handler, a handler error) is logged and left on the queue, so SQS redelivers it after the visibility timeout and, after the queue's maxReceiveCount, moves it to its dead-letter queue: give the queue one. --once drains what is queued and stops (exit code 1 if anything failed). An erasure prints one JSON line ({"forgot": <tenant>, "event": ..., "entities": ...}) on stdout for your audit log; everything else goes to stderr. KEEL_QUEUE and KEEL_DB stand in for the flags. Kafka has no per-message redelivery (committing a later offset skips a failed one), so it has no command yet; use KafkaAdapter from Python:

from keel.adapters.bus import KafkaAdapter, SqsAdapter

adapter = KafkaAdapter.connect("broker:9092", topic="keel-events", group_id="keel")
adapter = SqsAdapter.connect("https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/keel-events")
ingestor.ingest(adapter)            # drain what is there now, then stop
ingestor.ingest(adapter.follow())   # consume forever

Delivery is at-least-once: the offset is committed, or the SQS message deleted, only after the batch that holds it is committed (Ingestor.ingest calls the adapter's ack()), so a crash mid-batch redelivers the whole batch. With batch=N on SQS, keep the visibility timeout above the time a batch takes. A message that is not a valid envelope raises and stays on the bus; pass dead_letter=lambda body, error: ... to log it somewhere and move on. KafkaAdapter.connect(..., **config) merges extra keys into the confluent-kafka consumer config (dotted keys go through a dict: **{"security.protocol": "SSL"}); SqsAdapter.connect(queue_url, **kwargs) passes them to boto3.client("sqs", ...). connect also takes the adapter's own options as keywords: KafkaAdapter.connect(..., poll_timeout=1.0, dead_letter=...), SqsAdapter.connect(queue_url, batch_size=10, wait_seconds=10, dead_letter=...); or build the adapter from your own client with the same keywords: KafkaAdapter(consumer, ...), SqsAdapter(client, queue_url, ...). Both adapters only need two calls from their client (poll/commit, receive_message/delete_message), which is how the tests run them on fakes and how you would wrap another client.

docs.title: Serve the tools over MCP
docs.text:
uv sync --extra mcp
uv run keel serve examples/fleet --tenant acme-logistics --events examples/fleet/events.jsonl

With Claude Code, one command registers the server. The agent sees exactly five tools and nothing else:

claude mcp add keel -- uv run --directory $PWD keel serve examples/fleet --tenant acme-logistics --events examples/fleet/events.jsonl

With Codex CLI (OpenAI), declare the server in ~/.codex/config.toml. Keel annotates context, history, search and related as read-only, so Codex runs them without asking even under approval_policy = "never"; annotate writes, so it prompts unless you set default_tools_approval_mode = "auto" on the server:

[mcp_servers.keel]
command = "uv"
args = ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/keel", "keel", "serve", "examples/fleet", "--tenant", "acme-logistics", "--events", "examples/fleet/events.jsonl"]
startup_timeout_sec = 60

A headless run, for a smoke test or CI:

codex exec --json "Which tires on unit:MXK-4821 are critical according to the cartridge's own rules? Use only the keel tools." < /dev/null

Checked on 2026-10-14 with Codex CLI 0.162 and openai/gpt-5.2-codex behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway: seven calls (search, related, context, history with predicate=depth_mm), the right tire, the right depth on 2026-09-20, and the threshold quoted from the cartridge rather than assumed. Any other MCP client works the same way: a stdio server, five tools, one tenant per server instance. If the cartridge declares agents:, add --agent <id>: the server then reads and writes only what that agent may, and signs its annotations. Agent-scope memory is read only by the agent that wrote it, so a server started without --agent reads none.

Where is the graph stored?

In memory with --events: the server ingests the stream at start and serves it, which is enough for a demo. For a deployment, pass --db keel.db instead: a SQLite file (stdlib, WAL mode) that an ingest process fills while keel serve reads it. Or point --db at a MySQL or MariaDB you already run: --db mysql://user:password@host:3306/keel (mariadb:// is accepted too; uv sync --extra mysql); the tables are created on first use and the same conformance suite runs against it in CI. Sharing the database with your application: ?prefix=keel_ names the tables keel_entities, keel_facts, and so on. In code, the same option is a constructor argument: SqliteStore("keel.db", prefix="keel_"), MysqlStore.from_url(url, prefix="keel_") or MysqlStore(connect, prefix="keel_").

uv run keel ingest examples/fleet examples/fleet/events.jsonl --db keel.db   # or adapter.follow() in your own process
uv run keel serve examples/fleet --tenant acme-logistics --db keel.db
uv run keel replay examples/fleet examples/fleet/events.jsonl acme-logistics --db keel.db   # wipe one tenant, rebuild it from the log

The log is the truth and the file is derived: replay rebuilds one tenant from the external log (your outbox table, your bus, a .jsonl) and never from the file itself. What agents and people wrote through annotate, and consolidations of it, is not in the log, so replay keeps it and the events land around it. The store is pluggable: SqliteStore is the default, and any store that passes tests/test_store.py (see contributing) can take its place.

docs.title: Serve the tools over HTTP
docs.text:
For a backend, or for many tenants from one process, serve the same five operations as a JSON API (uv sync --extra http):

KEEL_SECRET=change-me uv run keel serve examples/fleet --transport http --db keel.db --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

The secret is read from KEEL_SECRET; --secret-env OTHER_VAR reads it from another variable. If the variable is unset, the server starts open only on a loopback host (127.0.0.1, the default, ::1 or localhost), with a warning. On any other --host it refuses to start unless you pass --allow-open, for when your own proxy authenticates every request.

Browse the graph. --ui also serves a read-only page at /ui: search a tenant, open a subject's context (optionally as of a past instant, with its rules evaluated), click a predicate for its history and a neighbour in the graph to walk to it. The page holds no data; it asks for the secret, the tenant and, when the cartridge declares agents, the agent, keeps them for the browser tab only, and reads through the same /v1 API, so every scope and registry rule applies. Off by default.

TLS and HTTP/2. --certfile and --keyfile (PEM; or KEEL_CERTFILE, KEEL_KEYFILE) serve https. --http2 runs the server on Hypercorn instead of uvicorn (uv sync --extra http2) and speaks HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 on the same port: h2 negotiated by ALPN over TLS, or cleartext h2c (prior knowledge or Upgrade) without it, which is what a proxy in front that talks h2c to its origin uses. HTTP/1.1 clients keep working. On the client side, keel.client.Client(..., http_client=httpx.Client(http2=True)) (SDKs).

KEEL_SECRET=change-me uv run keel serve examples/fleet --transport http --http2 --db keel.db \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --certfile cert.pem --keyfile key.pem
Call Body (? optional, default in parentheses) Returns POST /v1/events one envelope or a list the ingest report: processed, duplicates, unhandled, errors, forgotten, skipped POST /v1/context {"subject", "as_of"?, "depth"? (0), "as_known_at"?, "task"?, "detail"? ("full" or "concise")} what context returns POST /v1/history {"subject"?, "since"?, "until"?, "predicate"?, "scope"?, "as_known_at"?, "task"?, "changed_since"?, "limit"?} facts POST /v1/search {"text"? (""), "kind"?, "rule"?, "limit"?, "after"?, "mode"? ("text" or "semantic"), "min_score"?, "related_to"?, "via"?} entities and facts POST /v1/annotate {"subject", "predicate", "value", "scope"? ("task"), "evidence"?, "by"?, "task"?, "key"?, "status"?} the fact POST /v1/related {"subject", "relation"?, "as_of"?} neighbours GET /health {"ok", "cartridge", "mcp"} GET /openapi.json the contract, for generated clients

Times are ISO 8601 strings. Every request carries Authorization: Bearer $KEEL_SECRET, X-Keel-Tenant (optional when the server is bound with --tenant or KEEL_TENANT, which is then the default) and, when the cartridge declares agents, X-Keel-Agent. Your product authenticates its users and sets the two headers; Keel takes them as given and builds the tools for that tenant and agent per request. /health, /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc need no token. Two optional headers are stored with every write the request makes: traceparent (W3C trace context) and X-Keel-Tool-Call (the agent's tool call id).

On /v1/events, X-Keel-Tenant is optional: each envelope names its tenant, and when the header is present every envelope must match it. The agent registry does not apply to ingest.

Status Meaning 400 bad input: missing X-Keel-Tenant, an envelope of another tenant, an unknown rule, an invalid mode or detail 401 bad or missing bearer token 403 a refusal (scope policy, agent registry), with its reason 422 a malformed body, such as an envelope that fails validation

With --tenant, the same server also exposes /mcp (MCP over streamable HTTP) bound to that tenant, for agents that speak MCP and cannot run a local process.

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/context -H "Authorization: Bearer change-me" -H "X-Keel-Tenant: acme-logistics" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"subject": "tire:T-9001"}'

Reads follow the memory scopes. Agent-scope memory is read only by the agent that wrote it (send X-Keel-Agent to read your own). Task-scope memory tied to a task id is read only by calls that pass that task (history's task is an exact filter); task-scope memory with no task id belongs to the tenant. Global-scope memory lives in a reserved partition, __global__, that every tenant reads and no event may write; neither a tool call nor an envelope may use that tenant name.

docs.title: Run it in a container
docs.text:
ghcr.io/angelkurten/keel serves the tools over HTTP (/v1, and /mcp when KEEL_TENANT is set) on port 8000, for amd64 and arm64. Tags follow the releases: 0.24.0, 0.24, latest, and -slim variants without the Chroma client (a third of the size, no semantic search on Chroma). The cartridge is not in the image: mount it at /cartridge.

docker run -p 8000:8000 -e KEEL_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  -e KEEL_DB=mysql://keel:secret@db.internal:3306/keel \
  -v ./examples/fleet:/cartridge:ro -v keel-data:/data ghcr.io/angelkurten/keel:0.24.0
  • It refuses to start without KEEL_SECRET (or --allow-open behind your own auth proxy), since it listens on every interface.
  • /data is the working directory and a volume: a SQLite graph (KEEL_DB=/data/keel.db), the keel index cursor (/data/.keel/) and a .env live there.
  • It runs as an unprivileged user and checks its own /health (no curl needed in the image). Configuration is the environment (§ Configuration); every command reads KEEL_DB, KEEL_TENANT and KEEL_INDEX.
  • Any other command runs the same way: docker run ... ghcr.io/angelkurten/keel:0.24.0 index /cartridge (the entrypoint is keel).
  • To ship your cartridge inside, two lines: FROM ghcr.io/angelkurten/keel:0.24.0 and COPY cartridges/mine /cartridge.

deploy/docker-compose.yml runs Keel with its own MySQL, a Chroma server and keel index every 15 minutes: KEEL_SECRET=... docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d. docker build -t keel . builds this checkout; --build-arg KEEL_VERSION=0.24.0 builds a release from PyPI. deploy/smoke.sh <image> checks an image end to end.

docs.title: Semantic search
docs.text:
search(text, mode="semantic") finds subjects by meaning ("worn-out tyre" finds a tire at 2.6 mm), filtered by tenant, the agent's read slice, kind and rule. Two adapters, both replaceable: where vectors live and where embeddings come from.

uv sync --extra chroma        # only for the bundled Chroma adapter; Python 3.11+ (chromadb needs onnxruntime)
export KEEL_EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 KEEL_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small KEEL_EMBEDDINGS_API_KEY=...
uv run keel index examples/fleet --tenant acme-logistics --db keel.db --index chroma:///var/keel/vectors   # cron it: incremental
uv run keel serve examples/fleet --transport http --db keel.db --index chroma:///var/keel/vectors

keel index keeps the time of its last run in a cursor file and indexes only what changed since; --full rebuilds the tenant's index. The cursor sits next to a chroma:///path index (keel-index-<tenant>.cursor), else in .keel/index-<tenant>.cursor under the working directory; --cursor or KEEL_INDEX_CURSOR puts it elsewhere. In a container, keep it on the same volume as the index: a cursor lost on deploy makes the next run a full rebuild, and keel index says so when it starts without one. Embedding batches go out four at a time (--workers, KEEL_INDEX_WORKERS), and a rate limit or a 5xx from the embeddings API is retried with backoff. --all-tenants indexes every tenant in the store, each with its own cursor (--cursor-dir or KEEL_INDEX_CURSOR_DIR puts them all in one folder), and clears the documents of every tenant forgotten since its last run. One run per tenant at a time: a run that finds another holding the lock next to the cursor skips (two runs at once corrupt a Chroma index), so a cron that overlaps a slow run is safe. --embedder on index and serve picks where embeddings come from: openai (the default, configured by the KEEL_EMBEDDINGS_* variables), hash (deterministic, for tests) or your own pkg.module:factory?k=v. Use the same one for both.

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works for embeddings (OpenAI, OfoxAI, Azure, Ollama, vLLM).

chroma:///path opens the index inside the process. When keel serve and keel index run as separate processes (a server and a cron), the server does not see what the other process writes and searches fail with Error finding id. Run Chroma as a server and point both at it with chroma://host:port; keep chroma:///path for a single process or for tests.

The Chroma adapter ranks the lexical leg itself: it pulls a kind's documents once, keeps their BM25 in memory and reuses it until the collection's count changes or 300 seconds pass (ChromaIndex(bm25_ttl=...)), so a re-index by another process shows in the lexical leg within that time (the dense leg sees it at once). Each document carries its subject as metadata, so related_to filters inside Chroma; a collection built before 0.21 lacks it and filters after retrieval, slower, until one keel index --full.

Weaviate. uv sync --extra weaviate and --index weaviate://host:8080 (Weaviate 1.25 or later). Query parameters: grpc_port (default 50051), grpc_host (default the same host), secure=true for TLS on both, collection (default Keel); the API key comes from KEEL_WEAVIATE_API_KEY, never the URL. Keel uses one multi-tenant collection and makes each Keel tenant a Weaviate tenant, so the server isolates them. Vectors come from Keel's embedder (the collection has no vectorizer), and the lexical leg is Weaviate's own BM25, so nothing is pulled into Keel's memory and a re-index by another process shows at once. Its tokenizer splits cus-1974 into two words where Keel's keeps one, so lexical scores differ slightly from Chroma's. Run the conformance tests against a server with KEEL_WEAVIATE_URL=weaviate://localhost:8080 uv run pytest tests/test_semantic.py.

docs.title: Your own vector store or embedding model
docs.text:
Another vector database (pgvector, Qdrant, Pinecone, OpenSearch...) or your own model is an adapter you write: a plain class, nothing to inherit or register. examples/custom_adapters.py is a complete, tested one, a vector index on SQLite and an embedder wrapping any encode function. Run it with uv run python examples/custom_adapters.py.

class MyIndex:                                                     # keel.semantic.VectorIndex
    def upsert(self, tenant, items): ...                           # items: [(subject key, vector, document)]
    def delete(self, tenant, keys): ...
    def query(self, tenant, vector, k, where=None): ...            # [(key, cosine)], best first, this tenant only
    def clear(self, tenant): ...

class MyEmbedder:                                                  # keel.semantic.Embedder
    def embed(self, texts, role="document"): ...                   # one vector per text, same dimension

The rules an index must keep: every call is scoped by tenant and never returns another tenant's keys; query returns (key, score) with the score a cosine in [-1, 1], best first, at most k. Two capabilities are optional and detected from the signature: where={"kind": [...]} on query filters inside the index (without it Keel filters after retrieval, which an approximate index can miss), and a text_query(tenant, text, k, where=None) method adds the lexical leg for hybrid search. An embedder that takes role gets "query" for questions and "document" for what it indexes.

Name them by a spec, module:factory?param=value (parameters arrive as text), on index and serve alike, and check them with the same conformance suite as the bundled adapters:

uv run keel index examples/fleet --tenant acme-logistics --db keel.db \
  --index "examples.custom_adapters:make_index?path=vectors.db" --embedder examples.custom_adapters:make_embedder
KEEL_VECTOR_INDEX="examples.custom_adapters:make_index?path=/tmp/v.db" KEEL_EMBEDDER=examples.custom_adapters:make_embedder \
  uv run pytest tests/test_semantic.py

Vectors you already compute. Keel embeds the document it renders for each subject (key, attributes, open facts, the relations the cartridge names) and the query text, with the same embedder, so both sides live in one vector space. It does not take precomputed vectors. To use your own model, wrap it as the embedder: a function from texts to vectors is enough (ModelEmbedder in the example). Vectors you computed elsewhere, from other text, would not match the documents Keel searches.
